INPATIENT DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Cardiology & Internal Medicine — Hospital Course

& Plan

Documented Allergies: Penicillin (anaphylaxis) and Ibuprofen (bronchospasm).

Hospital Course & Clinical Presentation

64-year-old female with non-valvular atrial fibrillation, chronic kidney disease stage 3b, and

community-acquired lower respiratory tract infection admitted with acute palpitations, productive

cough, and fever of 38.9 °C. Treated with intravenous antimicrobial therapy and rate-control

stabilization with full clinical recovery prior to discharge.

Discharge Vital Signs & Baseline Labs

Blood Pressure Heart Rate Temperature Serum Potassium & Creatinine

124/76 mmHg | 82 bpm (controlled AF) | 36.8 °C | K+ 5.7 mEq/L, Creatinine 1.9 mg/dL

Discharge Diagnoses

1. Non-valvular atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response.

2. Resolving community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

3. Chronic kidney disease stage 3b with mild hyperkalemia.

Discharge Medications

Warfarin 5 mg orally once daily in the evening for stroke prophylaxis.

Aspirin 81 mg orally once daily in the morning (verify concurrent anticoagulation indication).

Azithromycin 500 mg orally once daily for 3 days to complete respiratory course.

Ondansetron 4 mg orally every 8 hours as needed for nausea.

Pantoprazole 40 mg orally once daily before breakfast for 30 days.

Outpatient Follow-Up Investigations

Prothrombin time and INR (PT/INR) in 3 days.

Repeat serum potassium, serum sodium, and serum creatinine in 48 hours.

Complete blood count (CBC) and C-reactive protein (CRP) at 1-week follow-up.

Follow-up chest X-ray (PA view) and 12-lead ECG in 2 weeks.

INPATIENT DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Cardiology & Internal Medicine — Hospital Course

& Plan

Documented Allergies: Penicillin (anaphylaxis) and Ibuprofen (bronchospasm).

Hospital Course & Clinical Presentation

64-year-old female with non-valvular atrial fibrillation, chronic kidney disease stage 3b, and

community-acquired lower respiratory tract infection admitted with acute palpitations, productive

cough, and fever of 38.9 °C. Treated with intravenous antimicrobial therapy and rate-control

stabilization with full clinical recovery prior to discharge.

Discharge Vital Signs & Baseline Labs

Blood Pressure Heart Rate Temperature Serum Potassium & Creatinine

124/76 mmHg | 82 bpm (controlled AF) | 36.8 °C | K+ 5.7 mEq/L, Creatinine 1.9 mg/dL

Discharge Diagnoses

1. Non-valvular atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response.

2. Resolving community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

3. Chronic kidney disease stage 3b with mild hyperkalemia.

Discharge Medications

Warfarin 5 mg orally once daily in the evening for stroke prophylaxis.

Aspirin 81 mg orally once daily in the morning (verify concurrent anticoagulation indication).

Azithromycin 500 mg orally once daily for 3 days to complete respiratory course.

Ondansetron 4 mg orally every 8 hours as needed for nausea.

Pantoprazole 40 mg orally once daily before breakfast for 30 days.

Outpatient Follow-Up Investigations

Prothrombin time and INR (PT/INR) in 3 days.

Repeat serum potassium, serum sodium, and serum creatinine in 48 hours.

Complete blood count (CBC) and C-reactive protein (CRP) at 1-week follow-up.

Follow-up chest X-ray (PA view) and 12-lead ECG in 2 weeks.
